validity.recommendation: no action -- existence, classification, and duplicate status all confirmed
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE check. Sabal Trail is a very well-documented, real, in-service interstate gas transmission pipeline (FERC docket CP15-17, part of the Southeast Market Pipelines Project with Florida Southeast Connection and Transco's Hillabee Expansion). Confirmed independently via: EIA 'Today in Energy' (govt, https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=31972), the FERC 2014 Notice of Intent published in the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2014/02/26/2014-04046/...), Argus Media trade press, AP wire (WCTV), Wikipedia, and the operator's (Enbridge/Sabal Trail Transmission LLC) own sites. Correctly classified: interstate natural gas transmission pipeline (not gathering/gas processing), Fuel=Gas is trivially correct. DUPLICATE check against the 37-PID Gulf Coast roster: P2606 is ALSO named 'Sabal Trail Gas Transmission Pipeline' (len=0.0, cap=170.00) -- this is NOT a duplicate of P0249. EIA's July 2017 article states Sabal Trail's Phase II (compressor-station additions only, completed 2020) added exactly 170 MMcf/d of capacity with no new pipe -- this matches P2606's Capacity=170.00 and explains why its LengthKnown=0 (compression-only expansion, correctly coded per the 'no new physical pipe -> LengthKnown=0' rule). See cross_row_leads. Also note: EIA describes a Phase III (2021, +70 MMcf/d, compressor upgrades only) that does NOT appear to have its own PID in the 37-row roster provided -- flagging as a possible gap for the orchestrator to check, not fabricating a new row.

Status='operating' is well-supported by context (status is inferable per url_verifier guidance, not a literal string match). EIA states FERC authorized full operation on July 3, 2017; Sabal Trail's own current 'About' page (2026) describes the line as presently in service ('is capable of transporting...'); Argus Media's contemporaneous 2017 piece covers the start of service. All independent origins (US government / operator / trade press).
Trivially confirmed: every source describes this as a natural gas pipeline. Enbridge's own factsheet lists 'Products transported: Natural gas'; EIA calls it an 'interstate natural gas pipeline'.

Confirmed as a transmission trunk, not a gathering/feeder line. The FERC 2014 Notice of Intent (Federal Register) describes it as '...natural gas transmission pipeline and associated facilities'; EIA independently calls it an 'interstate natural gas pipeline'. Two independent origins (FERC/Federal Register vs. EIA -- different agencies, different processes).

validity.recommendation: verify ProposalYear against the original FERC certificate application filing date -- current sourcing is thin
validity.researcher_notes: ProposalYear=2011 could NOT be independently corroborated to 2+ sources. The only source found stating anything about a pre-2013 origin is Wikipedia's uncited line 'The pipeline has been being planned since before 2011' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabal_Trail_Transmission_Pipeline) -- vague, and Wikipedia's own article carries no footnote for that specific sentence. Meanwhile the well-documented, well-sourced public milestone is FPL's July 26, 2013 announcement that it had selected Sabal Trail Transmission LLC and Florida Southeast Connection LLC to build the pipeline after an RFP process (newsroom.fpl.com/2013-07-26-FPL-selects-Sabal-Trail-Transmission-and-Florida-Southeast-Connection-to-build-new-natural-gas-pipeline-system-into-Florida -- I did not verify/cite this FPL newsroom URL directly since it wasn't run through url_verifier, but multiple secondary sources corroborate the July 2013 selection date). Sabal Trail's actual FERC application (docket CP15-17) was filed in 2015. So there are at least two candidate 'proposal' milestones on the public record -- an unsourced 'before 2011' planning claim, and a well-documented 2013 RFP-award / 2015 FERC-filing sequence -- and none of them cleanly land on 2011. Flagging rather than silently passing per standing rule 4/corollary (d).

Confirmed by three independent origins: Duke Energy's May 2015 press release ('The pipeline, scheduled to begin service in 2017...'); EIA's July 10, 2017 'Today in Energy' article stating FERC authorized full Phase I operation on July 3, 2017; and Argus Media's contemporaneous trade-press coverage of the service start. High tier, well corroborated.

validity.recommendation: verify Capacity/CapacityUnits against the original FERC certificate (docket CP15-17) -- likely a units conflation between MMcf/d and Dth/d, not just rounding
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Capacity=830.00, CapacityUnits=MMcf/d for Phase I. EIA's July 10, 2017 'Today in Energy' article (US government, independent of the operator) states explicitly: 'Sabal Trail Phase I is designed to have a total capacity of 810 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d)' -- a different figure, in the SAME unit GEM uses (MMcf/d), not just a unit-conversion artifact. Separately, offshore-technology.com (a trade publication) states the Phase I capacity as 'approximately 830,000 dekatherms a day (Dth/day)' -- note Dth, not MMcf. Natural gas typically runs ~1.02-1.03 MMBtu(Dth) per Mcf, so 810 MMcf/d x ~1.025 =~ 830,000 Dth/d -- i.e. the 810-MMcf/d and 830,000-Dth/d figures plausibly describe the SAME underlying capacity in two different units (volumetric vs. energy-content), not a genuine disagreement on the physical capacity. That makes GEM's cell -- '830.00' explicitly labeled 'MMcf/d' -- look like it may have inherited the 830 figure from a Dth/d source without the unit conversion, which would overstate the true MMcf/d capacity by ~2.5%. The original 2014 FERC Notice of Intent (Federal Register, an independent regulatory source) gives yet a third, earlier planning-stage figure: 'an initial capacity of 800,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d)'. None of the three sources found state '830 MMcf/d' outright. Flagging as a spec concern rather than silently passing -- recommend the researcher pull the actual FERC certificate order (CP15-17) or Sabal Trail's tariff for the authoritative Phase I design capacity and confirm the correct unit label.

Not a material disagreement -- normal as-planned-vs-as-built rounding across a multi-year construction project.

validity.recommendation: no action -- StartLocation/EndLocation (Alexander City, AL -> Reunion, FL) confirmed exactly
validity.researcher_notes: Confirmed at city-level, not just state-level. An Associated Press wire story (republished by WCTV; also republished by ABC Action News -- same wire story, one origin) states verbatim: 'The pipeline runs from Alexander City, Alabama, to Reunion, Florida.' Independently, a 2026 PHMSA special-permit letter (Docket PHMSA-2021-0052, Wayback-archived since the live PHMSA URL 403s to scripted clients) authorizes operation of the 36-inch Line 1 'from the outlet of Dunnellon compressor station (MP 395.73) to the inlet of the Reunion compressor station (MP 482.3)' -- independently confirming a real, named 'Reunion' compressor station exists on this exact pipeline at its Florida end. EIA (govt, third origin) corroborates at county level: 'from an interconnection with the Transco pipeline in Tallapoosa County, Alabama, to the Central Florida Hub in Osceola County, Florida' (Alexander City is the Tallapoosa County seat; Reunion is a community in Osceola County). StartState=Alabama and EndState=Florida both confirmed.

validity.recommendation: no action -- SegmentCost=$3.2B USD confirmed, though quoted precision varies by source/date
validity.researcher_notes: An Associated Press wire story (republished by WCTV, Feb 2017; same story also republished by ABC Action News -- one origin) states the figure exactly as GEM records it: '$3.2B Sabal Trail pipeline'. Earlier estimates from Duke Energy's own May 2015 press release ('the proposed and previously announced $3-billion Sabal Trail...pipeline') and offshore-technology.com both round to '$3 billion'. This is consistent, ordinary cost-estimate refinement over the ~2015-2017 construction period, not a material disagreement -- but note only ONE distinct origin (the AP wire) states the precise $3.2B figure GEM uses; the $3B figures are a different, earlier, rounder estimate. Searched SEC 10-K/10-Q filings (Duke Energy, Enbridge) for an exact capitalized-cost figure but did not pull the specific dollar amount from those filings in the time available -- a second precise-figure source is still owed if a reviewer wants to tighten this beyond 'consistent range'.

validity.recommendation: no action -- Owner1='Sabal Trail Transmission LLC' 100% matches the operator's own stated convention; optionally enrich with sub-entity percentages
validity.researcher_notes: At first glance 'Owner1 = Sabal Trail Transmission LLC, 100%' looks tautological (the project company owning itself) and I flagged it as a likely attribution error going in. It is NOT an error: Enbridge's own factsheet PDF states, verbatim, 'Ownership: Sabal Trail Transmission, LLC (100%), a joint venture of Enbridge, NextEra Energy, Inc., and Duke Energy Corporation' -- i.e. the operator itself uses exactly this convention (the SPV as 100% legal owner-of-record, with the JV partners described in prose rather than as separate cap-table rows). GEM's cell matches this exactly. For completeness: the underlying JV partner percentages have been reported differently at different times -- Duke Energy's own May 2015 press release states Duke Energy 7.5%, NextEra Energy 33%, Spectra Energy 59.5% (at acquisition); multiple 2016-2018 Duke Energy SEC 10-Q filings (post Spectra-to-NextEra partial sell-down) report Spectra Energy Partners LP (later Enbridge) 50%, NextEra Energy 42.5%, Duke Energy 7.5%. If the researcher wants sub-entity granularity (Owner2/3/4 with percentages) rather than the single 100% SPV row, the most recent SEC-filed split (Enbridge 50% / NextEra 42.5% / Duke 7.5%) is the one to use -- flagging as an option, not forcing the change since the current value is not wrong.

Searched FERC's 2014 Notice of Intent and the 2020 Final EIS for a whole-system design MAOP and did not find one stated in the sections read. UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating/generalizing a single-segment number to the whole pipeline.

The only lead found is an RBN Energy analyst article ('Mainline Florida - Sabal Trail, Marcellus/Utica Natural Gas Supply and Florida's Growing Power Market', 2017) whose headline and metadata assert Marcellus/Utica shale gas as the supply source, but the full body is subscriber-only/paywalled (confirmed via the Wayback copy's own schema.org markup: isAccessibleForFree=False) -- I could not read enough of the actual text to verify it names THIS pipeline with the supporting detail, so per rule 3 I am not citing it. Checked the FERC 2014 NOI and the EIA July 2017 'Today in Energy' article (both otherwise heavily used above) for upstream-basin language and found none. Leaving UNRESOLVED; the RBN Energy piece (or a Transco-system supply-point filing) is the lead to chase next, ideally via institutional/paid access.

cross_row_leads.facts: EIA (July 10, 2017): Sabal Trail Phase II, completed 2020, added 170 MMcf/d of capacity via two new compressor stations only -- no new pipeline mileage. This matches P2606 (same pipeline name in the roster, Capacity=170.00, LengthKnown=0.0) exactly and confirms LengthKnown=0 is the CORRECT coding for that row (compression-only expansion). Also note: EIA describes a Phase III (2021, +70 MMcf/d, compressor upgrades only, bringing system total to 1,050 MMcf/d) that does not appear to have its own PID anywhere in the 37-row Gulf Coast roster provided to me -- possible gap worth checking, not something I created a row for.

summary: P0249 (Sabal Trail) is real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate (P2606 is its legitimate Phase II sibling, not an overlap); 9 units confirmed high/medium, 2 flagged as spec concerns (ProposalYear=2011 is weakly sourced against a better-documented 2013 RFP-award date; Capacity=830 MMcf/d likely conflates a Dth/d figure with MMcf/d -- EIA independently states 810 MMcf/d for the same phase), 2 fills sourced (ConstructionYear=2016, Operator=Enbridge), 2 UNRESOLVED (Pressure -- only a segment-specific PHMSA MAOP found; FuelSource -- lead exists but is paywalled).
